comparator.name: Science, Technology & Innovation
comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA 2026–2027 bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme is 180 EC over three years. Year 1 lists twelve components totaling 60 EC across quantitative skills, digital methods, materials, life science, energy, food systems and professional research skills. The generic target requires a 54-EC year-2 specialisation; High-tech Designer Materials is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break, followed by the common 6-EC Design Project. Year 3 contains 30 EC genuine free choice, 12 EC Advanced Ethical Prototyping and an 18-EC Bachelor Project. The current page identifies the 2026–2027 digital study guide and explains that the bachelor project is three months of independent research recorded in a thesis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first programme is the closest feasible broad response to the selected materials-focused route while retaining the degree’s sustainability and design identity. Digital modelling/prototyping and life/health engineering are independently evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions that differ by well over 30 EC. A standalone Sustainability & Circularity route remains evidenced but is not attempted after reaching the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address material chemistry and properties, although UCR focuses on circular recovery and remediation.
Both integrate physics, chemistry, materials science and modelling around material behaviour.
Both address renewable-energy technology and technical system design.
Both require an applied research project with an external or practical scientific context; the UvA bachelor project is larger and individually thesis-based.
No selected UCR course provides a sufficiently direct one-to-one counterpart to the full Innovative Food Systems component.
The shared function is critical and responsible evaluation of advanced technological prototypes; the UvA component is broader and larger.
Both connect data handling and digital analysis to scientific applications.
Both introduce the digital and programming foundations used in later technical projects.
Both provide quantitative mathematical foundations for scientific analysis.
Both deepen quantitative skills needed for modelling and simulation.
Both introduce cellular, molecular and biochemical building blocks of living systems.
Both connect biochemical building blocks to practical life-science applications.
Both develop collaboration, reflection, communication and research-oriented professional skills.
Both centre iterative design work that develops a concrete product or prototype.
The UCR course develops evidence-based public communication and collaboration around climate and energy questions.
No selected UCR course provides a sufficiently direct one-to-one counterpart to the full Specialisation High-tech Designer Materials component.

notes.text: UvA Science, Technology & Innovation combines dedicated makerspace prototyping, engineering projects and a 54-EC technical specialisation. UCR can assemble strong science, data, sustainability, product-design and research pathways, but it does not reproduce the same continuous engineering studio, materials laboratory or 54-EC named track. The UCR alternatives therefore show defensible related programmes, not professional engineering equivalence.
